name: Castlevania - The Arcade
desc:
Castlevania: The Arcade is an arcade game, part of the Castlevania franchise by Konami. The game was announced on July 23, 2008. The game was released in Japan on October 2, 2009. A European release was announced for 2009 but only appeared at test locations in 2008.
The gameplay is similar to light gun shooters such as The House of the Dead. Players utilize a special LED whip remote. The remote has two buttons. A top thumb button used to activate the whip, prompting players to swing the remote at the screen to damage enemies. A bottom button for the index finger is used to activate subweapons, such as knives or crosses. Subweapons are refilled by collecting hearts (up to 25) strewn about each stage in the form of destructible candles and wooden crates.
Up to two players can play the game at once. Characters in the game include the Vampire Hunter, the Lady Gunner, and the Little Witch.

name: Crazy Streets (Thrill Drive 4)
desc:
Crazy Streets: Thrill Drive (also known as Thrill Drive 4) is a racing arcade game developed by Konami and released in 2007. It is the fourth entry in the Thrill Drive series, known for its high-speed traffic weaving and spectacular, often "creepy" crashes
The game is considered a "lost" arcade title because it was extremely rare and primarily saw limited location testing, particularly in the US.

name: GTI Club - Supermini Festa
desc:
GTI Club Supermini Festa! twin marks the return of a classic racing arcade game machine series. Like the original, players race small cars including the Mini Cooper. There are also a range of minigames for up to 4 players.
Rather than focusing on sports cars and high speed, in GTI Club Supermini Festa! it is more about using your driving skills and handbrake to navigate through tough tracks. Like the original GTI Club, players must find shortcuts and alternative routes to get through the course as quickly as possible to beat their rivals.
Race types include "Battle Race" and "Variety Battle". Variety battle allows up to four players to face off against one another in driving based minigames. In 'Tag' mode, one player is randomly selected at the beginning of the course to carry a bomb on top of their car. The player with the bomb must ram into other cars to 'tag' them and offload the bomb. A timer counts down during play, and when the timer reaches zero the bomb explodes and that player is eliminated.
Another minigame type is the Soccer mode, where players use their cars to hit a giant soccer ball into the goal. Once the timer reaches zero, the player with the highest score is the winner.

name: Lethal Enforcers 3
desc:
Lethal Enforcers 3 is a light gun game for one or two players, and it is the final in the Lethal Enforcers series. The game uses 3D polygon graphics instead of digitised actors.
The players move through the stages on-rails while shooting enemies. While running through the stages players can take cover behind a shield, which also reloads. Rack up combos for bonus points by consecutively hitting targets without missing. When innocent people are shot the players are demoted in rank and news paper headlines fill the screen.
The game has 6 distinct stages, each with its own title logo and short introduction similar to a tv show:
Cops in the city, fight the mob in the Akihabara district
Coast intrudes, enter a ship and fight drug smugglers in the harbor area
Rival Heat, round up gun smugglers in a subway station and tunnels
Airport 2004, hostage situation around a grounded airplane
Justice and Judgement, terrorists threaten to blow up a nuclear power plant
Lethal Enforcers 3, rescue the captured Prime Minister in a coup d'état

name: Road Fighters 3D
desc:
Road Fighters is the Japan-only sequel to the original Road Fighter, released in arcades in 2010. The game features 3D-enhanced graphics, with a mounted pair of goggles used to view the effect. Tracks are set in real-life locations and are all based on race courses from previous Konami racing titles, including Enthusia Professional Racing and the GTI Club series. The game includes numerous licensed vehicles, which can be saved using Konami's e-AMUSEMENT Pass containing tuning and customization data. This game is Konami's answer to Sega's Initial D Arcade Stage 4 and Namco's Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune in terms of card-based games, or Taito's Chase H.Q. 2 in terms of rebooted sequels.
Its opening theme "Take Me Higher" was composed (together with the system music) by Sota Fujimori and it was included on beatmania IIDX 18 Resort Anthem as a playable song. In addition, the game includes music from beatmania IIDX and Dance Dance Revolution series, as a form to promote another Konami arcade games.

name: Silent Hill The Arcade
desc:
The game takes place in 1993, when a group of five students and members of an occult club travel to Silent Hill to solve the mystery of Toluca Lake. It is known that seventy-five years ago a boat called "Little Baroness" disappeared with all the crew and passengers on the lake, and the bodies have never been found. The next morning after the arrival, students Eric and Tina (the protagonists) discover that one of their club members is injured while others are missing, and that the whole town is crawling with monsters.
Silent Hill: The Arcade is a rail shooter in the vein of The House of the Dead games, complete with off-screen reloading and weapon power-ups. The players will shoot down hordes of monsters in various familiar (and not so) locations including Brookhaven Hospital, Silent Hill Historical Society, Lakeside Amusement Park etc., on their way to the heart of the catastrophe — a little girl aboard the Little Baroness. The game features four endings, one them being a traditional "UFO" ending.
